analysis:
The PR changes docs/reference/protocol-messages.md only: the date bump on line 3 and a new "Close codes and the reconnect wait" section (head lines 173-190) describing how the provider chooses its reconnect delay from the WebSocket close code. The supplied units are unchanged surrounding head text (lines 583-1236) covering performance measurements, service reservation release, model replace, prefix cache v2 receipts and inference_request fields. They contain no new changes beyond the patch.

Security review of the new section: code 1012 picks a delay from serviceRestartDelayRange without growing the backoff. Any other close, or none, uses ExponentialBackoff. A session open for stableSessionDuration or longer, counted from its register frame, resets the backoff. Every reconnect sends a fresh register, so registration and attestation are not skipped or weakened. This is documentation only and changes no code, auth, attestation, encryption or key custody.

Relevant threat IDs: TB-002 and the availability assumptions. A malicious or compromised coordinator, or an on-path party able to forge a close frame, could steer reconnect timing with 1012. The coordinator is trusted, and the delay is bounded by a range. The section does not give the range values, which sit in the cli-reference runtime constants and the Swift policy file, neither supplied. Unverified contract: whether serviceRestartDelayRange is bounded and jittered, and whether the stable-session reset can be abused to defeat backoff against a coordinator under load. This is a note for integration, not a finding.

The rest of the protocol text is context only. It already states fail-closed handling for cache receipts, nonce, sequence and connection binding, and model_replace fencing. Nothing in the diff alters those, so no regression is identified. No threat-model update is needed.
